content.overview: Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor, to be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution. Nothing in the article transfers to the Governor functions conferred by any existing law on any other authority, or prevents Parliament or the State Legislature from conferring functions by law on any authority subordinate to the Governor.
content.glance: State executive power vested in Governor (directly or through subordinates). Parallel to Union Art 53.
content.study:
Article 154 is the State counterpart of Article 53:
(1) Executive power of the State vested in the Governor; exercised directly or through subordinate officers in accordance with the Constitution.
(2) Does not transfer to the Governor functions conferred by existing law on other authorities; does not prevent Parliament or the Legislature of the State from conferring functions on authorities subordinate to the Governor.

Exercise is subject to the aid-and-advice framework of Article 163.

Examination: vesting in Governor; subordinates; no automatic transfer of existing statutory functions; legislative power to confer functions.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Executive power of the State vested in the Governor.
2. Exercise: directly or through officers subordinate to him, in accordance with the Constitution.
3. Does not transfer existing statutory functions from other authorities; does not prevent conferment of functions on subordinates by law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Where is the executive power of a State vested?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 154, the executive power of the State is vested in the Governor and is exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution. The article does not transfer to the Governor functions conferred by existing law on other authorities, and does not prevent Parliament or the State Legislature from conferring functions by law on authorities subordinate to the Governor.

examTips: Parallel to Art 53; Governor; subject to Art 163 aid and advice.

keyTakeaways: Art 154: State executive power vested in Governor.
